main_text.head: QVÆSTIO IGITVR DISCEPTATVR hæc: Quæstio.
AN JESUS CHRISTUS MERITO ET Satisfactione, ac sufficientis λύτρα pro peccatis nostris persolutione, tanquam Sponsor noster, salutem æternam nobis acquisierit?
main_text.p: Confessarium. An Christianus teneatur ad salutem suam credere, confidere & obedire Iesu Christo, ut servatori suo, qui ipsi salutem æternam, merito suo, & præstita satisfactione Deo Patri pro peccatis ipsius pepererit?
main_text.head: DECLARATIO QVÆSTIONIS.
main_text.p: Christus Dei Vnigenitus Filius. Observandum vero hic, nos statuere: 1. JESUM CHRISTUM esse Dei vivétis Filium unigenitum. (Matth. 16. dicit hic Jesus Discipulis: Vos autem quem me dicitis esse? Respondens vero Simon Petrus dixit: Tu es Christus Filius ille Dei viventis. Tunc respondens Jesus, dixit ei: Beatus es Simo Bar-jona, quia caro & sanguis hoc non retexit tibi, sed Pater meus, qui est in cœlis. Sed & ego

page.notes: Printing is an early 17th-century Latin text with Greek (λύτρα) and italic scripture quotations. The page number "ii" at top left is read as 11; the first character is uncertain. The marginal note beside the Confessarium paragraph is partly worn; "Confessarium." is a best reading. The mark "(Matth. 16." is an inline italic reference with an opening parenthesis left unclosed in print. The final word "dico" is the catchword at the lower right and is not repeated in the text. The question paragraph in small capitals is set as a heading-level passage, as it is the statement under the QVÆSTIO title.
